content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, the number to call is 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo laboratory and/or medical tests, such as monitoring sodium levels, as directed by your healthcare provider. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not freeze it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to reduce the acidity of urine. Less acidic urine helps the kidneys eliminate uric acid, which can prevent gout and certain types of kidney stones (urate stones). The active ingredients, citric acid and citrate salts (containing potassium and sodium), belong to a class of drugs known as urinary alkalinizers. Before each dose, shake the container well. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically four times a day. To minimize the risk of diarrhea and stomach upset, take each dose after a meal. Mix the prescribed dose in a full glass (4 to 8 ounces or 120 to 240 milliliters) of cold water or juice just before consuming it. Drink the entire mixture slowly. Refrigerating the mixture before drinking may improve its taste. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully and do not increase the dose or frequency without medical approval. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. While on this medication, you may need to test the pH (acidity) of your urine using special test paper to determine the appropriate dose. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach pain. Mixing the medication with water or juice, taking it after meals, and increasing fluid intake can help reduce these side effects. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may worsen high blood pressure during pregnancy (toxemia of pregnancy). It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams per day), continue taking it unless advised otherwise by your doctor.
